summary: Noisy background snapshot-sync causing gradual dedicated capacity thinning and p95 latency drift
description:
Issue summary:
Customer AtlasAI reports a gradual degradation in dedicated pool throughput over several days, culminating in an elevated p95 tail and increased attach latency for batched routes. Degradation correlates with a nightly background sync process that appears to increase IO/sidecar CPU and cause allocator attach retries.

Impact:
- ~35-50% drop in effective throughput for AtlasAI's reserved pool during 09:30-11:00 UTC windows.
- P95 latencies increased from baseline ~120ms to ~650ms for batched generation routes.
- Autoscaler shows oscillation (scale-up spikes followed by rapid cooldown).
- Customer experiencing increased 5xx attach failures and intermittent fallback routing to hosted variants.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (reserved) for AtlasAI, prod, region us-west-2.
- Model traffic primarily to redwood/gpt-medium-v1 and fallbacks to open/gptj-6b-quant.
- Observed during both weekday and weekend windows.

Steps to reproduce / Observed behavior:
1) Customer runs steady batched load during business hours.
2) At ~09:30 UTC a background service (snapshot-sync-service) kicks off heavy NVMe reads and sidecar CPU spikes (observed on node-level).
3) Allocator attach latency increases (attach RPC retries observed), autoscaler triggers additional nodes then rapidly scales back.
4) Batching queue grows, p95 and p99 latency jump; some requests fall back to hosted variants.

Expected behavior:
- Background maintenance jobs should not cause allocator attach latencies or degrade dedicated serving throughput.
- Autoscaler should avoid oscillatory scale actions when IO noise is transient.

Logs / Metrics / Artifacts:
- Grafana: dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/serve/dedicated-pool-overview?orgId=1&var-pool=atlasai
- Cloudwatch: NVMeIOps spike graph (node group atlasai-reserved-01) 2026-03-09 09:25-09:45 UTC.
- Allocator logs (sample): "attach_rpc_timeout: 2.3s retries=4" from allocator-03.
- Autoscaler events: repeated scale_up -> scale_down within 6m windows.
- Slack thread: #support channel: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C01SUPPORT/p1678520000

Customer impact notes:
- AtlasAI flagged multiple production jobs falling back to hosted endpoints which increased their costs and caused transient feature regressions for their users.

Requested action from Redwood:
- Investigate root cause for allocator attach latency correlated with NVMe/sidecar spikes.
- Provide immediate mitigation to stabilize dedicated throughput for AtlasAI during nightly sync windows (workaround preferred while permanent fix is planned).

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Snapshot-sync-sidecar NVMe read pressure + CPU saturation causes allocator attach RPCs to queue and timeout, leading to autoscaler overcompensation and batching backlog.
Confirmed node-level NVMe read IOPS spike coincident with attach error bursts (observed on allocator-02 and allocator-03) starting 2026-03-09.
Reproduced locally via stress test: running snapshot-sync imitation causes attach latency to increase and autoscaler to trigger scale-up rapidly.
Observed that sidecar process had no CPU QoS reservation; under IO pressure its event loop latency rises sharply.
Autoscaler config: current windows are too reactive for short-lived IO noise; smoothing and cooldown parameters need tuning for dedicated pools with noisy maintenance windows.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation applied: throttled snapshot-sync-service on atlasai nodegroup during peak window; results validated by customer (p95 reduced to ~180ms).
Cluster changes: sidecar CPU reservation increased to 200m for affected dedicated pools; implemented conservative allocator attach backoff to avoid tight retry loops.
Long-term actions assigned: ENG-4521 (IO isolation for maintenance jobs), ENG-4522 (autoscaler smoothing and dedicated pool heuristics), OPS-310 (runbook for scheduling snapshot jobs off-peak).
Follow-up: monitor dedicated pool for 72h; if oscillation persists revert to more aggressive isolation. Notify customer of roadmap and expected ETA for permanent fixes.
Customer communicated reduction in impact and requested postmortem once permanent mitigations are scheduled.
